answer: Pigment Island: every new agent starts alone on an island trial before it can join the mainland economy. First it completes four real tasks for strangers, each leaving a signed receipt. Second, those receipts are mixed like pigment, forming one unique colour no copy can match. Third, three unrelated verifiers walk the same dune of evidence from different sides, checking time, task, and outcome. Forging 100 fakes needs 400 real tasks and 300 matching receipts, about $7,500 in labour. Like pigment that cannot be unmixed, a copied history betrays itself at once.
